root_cause.text: In the RDMA/srp receive path, srp_process_rsp() trusted target-controlled SRP_RSP resp_data_len/sense_data_len fields and used rsp->data + resp_data_len as the sense-data source without validating that the header, response data, and sense region fit within the actual received length (wc->byte_len), causing an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes srp_process_rsp() to take byte_len from wc->byte_len and adds `if (sizeof(*rsp) + (u64)resp_len + sense_len <= byte_len)` before `memcpy`, while the CVE/commit explicitly states that `resp_data_len` was "never checked against the number of bytes actually received (wc->byte_len)" and that a large target-supplied value could make the sense copy source land past the receive buffer and fault.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a byte_len argument to srp_process_rsp() so response processing can use the received message length.
intent_record.what: The function signature of srp_process_rsp() was changed to add a new third parameter of type u32 named byte_len, with the declaration split across two lines for formatting.
intent_record.how: This enables callers to pass the received response length into srp_process_rsp() so the function can use the actual byte count during response handling, though no runtime behavior change is shown in this hunk by itself.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checking before copying SRP sense data to prevent out-of-bounds reads from truncated target responses.
intent_record.what: The code in srp_process_rsp() replaces an unconditional memcpy() of sense data based on rsp->resp_data_len and rsp->sense_data_len with local u32 variables for those lengths, adds a bounds check that verifies sizeof(*rsp) + resp_len + sense_len is no greater than byte_len before copying, switches the copy length expression to min(sense_len, SCSI_SENSE_BUFFERSIZE), and adds an error log that reports truncated sense data when the bounds check fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now copies SCSI sense data only when the response buffer actually contains the full response-data-plus-sense-data region indicated by target-provided lengths. This prevents reading past the end of the received buffer when a target reports lengths larger than the bytes received, and instead drops the malformed or truncated sense data while emitting an error message.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the received byte length into SRP response processing so responses can be handled using the actual message size.
intent_record.what: The call to srp_process_rsp() in srp_recv_done() was changed from passing two arguments, ch and iu->buf, to passing three arguments by adding wc->byte_len as the third parameter.
intent_record.how: At runtime, SRP response processing now receives the received work completion byte length, enabling srp_process_rsp() to use the actual message size when handling responses instead of operating without explicit length information.
